title: Get: Receiving, Becoming and Arriving
summary: Use get to describe receiving things, becoming different, arriving somewhere and getting into or out of vehicles. Learn which common expressions need a preposition.
learningObjectives: Use get + noun for receiving, buying, finding or obtaining something.
Describe a change with get + adjective and common expressions such as get ready and get lost.
Choose get to + place and get home/here/there without to.
Distinguish get in/out of a car from get on/off a bus or train.

explanation.heading: Get + a noun
explanation.body: Get with a noun can mean receive, obtain, buy or find, depending on the context. You can get a message, get some food or get a job. In everyday English, get a taxi or get a bus can also mean take that transport.
explanation.example: Did you get the photo I sent yesterday?

explanation.heading: Get + adjective means become
explanation.body: Use get followed by an adjective for a change of state: get hungry, get cold, get tired, get angry or get better. Getting shows that the change is happening now. Other frequent expressions include get married, get dressed and get lost.
explanation.example: The soup is getting cold, so let’s eat.

explanation.heading: Get to a place; get home without to
explanation.body: Use get to + place to say arrive: get to the station, get to work, get to the museum. Do not use to before home, here or there: get home, get here, get there.
explanation.example: We got to the hotel just before sunset.

explanation.heading: Getting into and out of vehicles
explanation.body: For a car or taxi, usually say get in or get into it and get out of it. For a bus, train or plane, usually say get on and get off. Use out of before a named car or taxi when leaving it.
explanation.example: We got off the train and got into a taxi.

left.label: Get + noun
left.example: Sam got a new coat yesterday.

right.label: Get + adjective
right.example: Sam got cold during the walk.
right.note: Got cold describes a change of condition.

comparisons.title: Entering a car versus boarding a bus

left.label: Get in a car
left.example: We got into the car outside the house.
left.note: Get in or get into is typical for cars and taxis.

right.label: Get on a bus
right.example: We got on the bus outside the house.
right.note: Get on is typical for buses, trains and planes.

examples.sentence: I got a parcel from my cousin this morning.
examples.note: Got a parcel means received it.

examples.sentence: Can you get some bread on your way back?
examples.note: Get some bread can mean buy or bring it.

examples.sentence: It got dark while we were walking.

examples.note: There is no to before home.

examples.sentence: The passengers got off the bus near the hospital.
examples.note: Get off is used when leaving a bus.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I got to home at nine.
commonMistakes.why: Get home has no to, unlike get to the station.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The tea is getting to cold.
commonMistakes.why: An adjective follows get directly: getting cold.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Liam got on the taxi and closed the door.
commonMistakes.correct: Liam got in the taxi and closed the door.
commonMistakes.why: Use get in for entering a taxi.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The driver got out the car.
commonMistakes.correct: The driver got out of the car.
commonMistakes.why: When you name a car after get out, add of.

studyTips: Look at the word after get: a noun often means receive or obtain; an adjective often means become.
Memorise the arrival pair: get to the office, but get home (not get to home).
Picture the vehicle: get in/out of a car; get on/off a bus or train.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: When you ___ a postcard, you receive it.
exercises.feedback: Get + noun can mean receive: get a postcard.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: The sky is getting ___ . Let’s go inside before the storm.
exercises.feedback: Get + adjective describes a change: getting dark.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct way to say we arrived at the museum: We ___ the museum at eleven.
exercises.feedback: Use got to + place to mean arrived at that place.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence correctly describes leaving a bus?
choices: We got off the bus at Market Street.
We got out the bus at Market Street.
We got in the bus at Market Street.
exercises.feedback: To leave a bus, use get off the bus.

exercises.prompt: Use a form of get: Can you ___ a loaf of bread on your way home?
acceptedAnswers: get
exercises.feedback: Get + noun can mean buy or collect something.

exercises.prompt: Use the past simple of get: It started raining, and we ___ wet because we had no coats.
acceptedAnswers: got

exercises.prompt: Use the past simple of get: We left at six and ___ to the airport at seven.
acceptedAnswers: got
exercises.feedback: Got to the airport means arrived there.

exercises.prompt: Complete the expression: The passengers got ___ the train at the first station and sat down.
acceptedAnswers: on
exercises.feedback: Use got on the train to describe boarding it.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I usually get to home before seven.
acceptedAnswers: I usually get home before seven.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: It is getting to dark outside.
acceptedAnswers: It is getting dark outside.
It's getting dark outside.
exercises.feedback: A describing adjective follows get directly: getting dark.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The driver got on the car and started the engine.
acceptedAnswers: The driver got in the car and started the engine.
The driver got into the car and started the engine.
exercises.feedback: For entering a car, use got in or got into, not got on.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: We got out the taxi near the station.
acceptedAnswers: We got out of the taxi near the station.
exercises.feedback: Add of when you name the vehicle after got out.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make a complete past simple sentence from these cues: Maya / get to / the office / at nine.
acceptedAnswers: Maya got to the office at nine.
speakingExercises.feedback: Get to becomes got to in the past simple.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change this sentence using getting: “The soup is becoming cold.”
acceptedAnswers: The soup is getting cold.
speakingExercises.feedback: Getting + adjective expresses a change in progress.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make a complete sentence from these cues: We / got off / the bus / outside the museum.
acceptedAnswers: We got off the bus outside the museum.
speakingExercises.feedback: Got off is the form for leaving a bus.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make a complete past-simple sentence from these cues: Max / get / a text message / this morning.
acceptedAnswers: Max got a text message this morning.
speakingExercises.feedback: Got a text message means received a message. Got is the past form of get.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change this statement into the past-simple negative, keeping the other words: “I got a letter yesterday.”
acceptedAnswers: I didn't get a letter yesterday.
I did not get a letter yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use did not or didn’t plus the base form get, not got, in a past-simple negative.

speakingExercises.prompt: A classmate asks, “When did Nora arrive here?” You know she arrived at eight. Answer in one sentence beginning “Nora” and using got here and at eight.
acceptedAnswers: Nora got here at eight.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use got here to mean arrived here. Do not add to before here.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct this sentence using the usual expression for boarding a train, keeping all other words: “The children got in the train at the main station.”
acceptedAnswers: The children got on the train at the main station.
speakingExercises.feedback: People normally get on a train or bus, but get in or into a car or taxi.

speakingExercises.prompt: Your friend is outside a taxi in the rain. Politely tell them to enter the taxi using “get in” or “get into”, and say it is warm inside. Use two short sentences, beginning with “Please”.
acceptedAnswers: Please get in the taxi. It's warm inside.
Please get in the taxi. It is warm inside.
Please get into the taxi. It's warm inside.
Please get into the taxi. It is warm inside.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use get in or get into with a taxi, and use it is or it’s to describe the warmth inside.

listeningExercises.audioText: I got a postcard from my uncle yesterday.
listeningExercises.feedback: Got a postcard means received a postcard.

listeningExercises.audioText: We got off the train at the final station.
listeningExercises.prompt: What did the people do at the final station?
listeningExercises.feedback: Got off the train means left the train.

listeningExercises.audioText: By the time we got home, everyone was asleep.
listeningExercises.prompt: Complete what you hear: “By the time we got ___, everyone was asleep.” Type one word.
acceptedAnswers: home
listeningExercises.feedback: Get home takes no to; home is the word heard.

listeningExercises.audioText: After looking for work all summer, Ben finally got a job in a café.
choices: He found a place to work.
listeningExercises.feedback: Got a job means Ben found employment; get plus a noun can mean obtain or find.

listeningExercises.audioText: The weather got colder during our walk, so we put on our coats.
listeningExercises.prompt: Why did they put on their coats?
choices: They were getting ready for bed.
listeningExercises.feedback: Got colder means the temperature decreased, so they needed warmer clothes.

listeningExercises.audioText: Tessa got on the bus, but Omar got into a taxi outside the station.
choices: In a car with a driver.
listeningExercises.feedback: Omar entered a taxi, while Tessa boarded a bus. Get into and get on distinguish the vehicles.

listeningExercises.audioText: My little sister is getting better after a week at home.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two words you hear immediately after “is”.
acceptedAnswers: getting better
listeningExercises.feedback: Getting better is get plus an adjective, describing an improvement in condition.

listeningExercises.audioText: When the taxi stopped, we got out of it near the museum.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two words you hear immediately after “got”.
acceptedAnswers: out of
listeningExercises.feedback: Get out of is the normal pattern for leaving a taxi or car.
